# Statistical methodology

## Long version (supplements, GitHub)

All analyses and visualizations were done in R @R. Statistical analyses were done using Bayesian hierarchical models implemented in R (version 4.4.3). Bayesian mixed-effects models were used as framework for meta-analysis since it provides coherent estimation of pooled effects, between-study heterogeneity, and predictive uncertainty; this approach is particularly advantageous when the number of included studies is limited . All models were fitted using the 'brms' package \[@brms-2\]. All models were fitted with at least 6,000 MCMC iterations per chain (including 2,000 warm-up iterations), using four chains per model. Posterior predictive checks were used to assess models fits. Model comparison was performed using approximate leave-one-out cross-validation with moment matching and exact refits for problematic observations as implemented in the 'loo' package [@loo-2]. Posterior summaries are reported as medians with 95% credible intervals defined by the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of the posterior distribution.

Prevalence of EHC was analysed using a hierarchical binomial model with a logit link. For each study $j$, the number of patients with EHC $y_j$ was modelled as $y_j \sim \mathrm{Binomial}(n_j, p_j)$, where $n_j$ denotes the number of patients in the study and $p_j$ the underlying prevalence. Between-study heterogeneity was modelled using a study-specific random intercept on the logit scale, $\mathrm{logit}(p_j) = \alpha + u_j$, with $u_j \sim \mathcal N(0, \tau^2)$. Between-study heterogeneity in prevalence was quantified using the posterior distribution of $\tau$, representing the standard deviation of the random intercepts on the logit scale. In addition, an approximate latent-scale intraclass correlation coefficient was calculated as $I^2 = \tau^2 / (\tau^2 + \pi^2/3)$, reflecting the proportion of total variance in the linear predictor attributable to between-study heterogeneity. To aid interpretation, a 95% predictive interval for the true underlying prevalence in a new study was derived by simulating study-specific random effects from $\mathcal N(0, \tau^2)$ and transforming the resulting linear predictors to the prevalence scale.

The number of EHC vessels per patient was analysed using a Poisson mixed-effects model with log-link. Let $Y_j$ denote the total number of EHC vessels observed in study $j$. We modelled $Y_j \sim \mathrm{Poisson}(\mu_j)$ with $\log(\mu_j) = \alpha + u_j + \log(n_j)$, where $\log(n_j)$ was included as an offset to model the expected count per patient and $u_j \sim \mathcal N(0, \tau^2)$ captured between-study heterogeneity on the log-rate scale. The pooled estimate corresponds to the expected number of EHC vessels per patient in a typical study. Between-study heterogeneity in EHC counts was summarised using the posterior distribution of $\tau$ on the log scale and by a Poisson variance partition coefficient (VPC), defined as the proportion of total variance in the outcome attributable to between-study variability. The VPC was estimated using posterior simulation based on the fitted model. A 95% predictive interval for the true underlying EHC count per patient in a new study was obtained by simulating new study-level random effects. As a sensitivity analysis, negative binomial mixed-effects models were fitted to allow for residual overdispersion beyond between-study heterogeneity. However, the negative binomial model did not improve predictive performance and exhibited unstable estimation of the dispersion parameter with frequent divergent transitions; therefore, the Poisson specification was retained.

The distribution of specific arterial sources of EHC was analyzed using two separate Bayesian hierarchical multinomial logistic regression models to assess different levels of anatomical granularity: (1) a coarse classification into 6 major arterial groups and (2) a detailed classification into 22 specific arterial branches. 
For each study $j$, the vector of counts $\mathbf{y}_j = (y_{j,1}, \dots, y_{j,K})$ for $K$ arterial categories was modeled as $\mathbf{y}_j \sim \mathrm{Multinomial}(n_j, \mathbf{p}_j)$, where $n_j$ is the total number of EHCs in study $j$ and $\mathbf{p}_j$ is the vector of underlying proportions. To account for between-study heterogeneity, study-specific random intercepts were included for each non-reference category on the logit scale:$\log\left(\frac{p_{j,k}}{p_{j,\mathrm{ref}}}\right) = \alpha_k + u_{j,k}$.
The inferior phrenic artery served as the reference category, and $u_{j,k} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \tau_k^2)$ represents the study-specific random effect for category $k$. To improve model convergence and ensure stable estimation—particularly for rare arterial sources with zero observed counts in some studies, we employed "data-driven" weakly informative priors for the global intercepts $\alpha_k$. These priors were centered on the log-odds of the overall empirical proportions across all studies, using a Laplace-like smoothing adjustment: $\alpha_k \sim \text{Student-t}(3, \mu_{\text{prior}}, 100)$, where $\mu_{\text{prior}} = \log((n_k + 0.01) / (n_{\text{ref}} + 0.01))$. Between-study standard deviations were assigned $\tau_k \sim \text{Exponential}(1)$ priors.
Pooled proportions were derived by transforming global intercepts to the probability scale using the softmax function. Heterogeneity for each arterial source was quantified by the category-specific standard deviation $\tau_k$ on the logit scale and a latent-scale intraclass correlation coefficient, $I^2_k = \tau_k^2 / (\tau_k^2 + \pi^2/3)$. These measures reflect the proportion of total variability in the linear predictor attributable to between-study differences for a given category relative to the reference. For the reference category, $\tau_k$ and $I^2_k$ are not defined under this parameterization. Finally, 95% predictive intervals (PIs) for the proportions in a new study were calculated by simulating new study-level random effects, accounting for the compositional nature of the data.

## Short version (manuscript body)

All analyses and visualizations were done in R @R. Statistical analyses were done using Bayesian hierarchical models implemented in R (version 4.4.3). Bayesian mixed-effects models as framework for meta-analysis since it provides coherent estimation of pooled effects, between-study heterogeneity, and predictive uncertainty; this approach is particularly advantageous when the number of included studies is limited. All models were fitted using the 'brms' package \[@brms-2\]. Posterior summaries are reported as medians with 95% credible intervals defined by the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of the posterior distribution. Models fits were assessed using posterior predictive checks.

EHC prevalence was analysed using a hierarchical binomial model with a logit link and a study-specific random intercept. Between-study heterogeneity was quantified using the posterior distribution of the standard deviation of the study-level random intercepts, representing variability in prevalence across studies beyond binomial sampling error. In addition, heterogeneity was summarised using an approximate latent-scale intraclass correlation coefficient, reflecting the proportion of total variability attributable to between-study differences. A predictive interval was derived by simulating new study-level random effects from the fitted model to characterise the expected range of the true underlying prevalence in a new study.

The number of EHC vessels per patient was analysed using a Poisson mixed-effects model with a log link and an offset for the number of patients. Between-study heterogeneity was quantified using the posterior distribution of the standard deviation of the random intercepts on the log-rate scale and further summarised using a Poisson variance partition coefficient (VPC), defined as the proportion of total variance attributable to between-study variability. A predictive interval was obtained by simulating new study-level random effects from the fitted model to describe the expected range of the true underlying EHC count per patient in a new study.

The distribution of specific arterial sources for EHC was analysed using a hierarchical multinomial model, which accounts for the compositional nature of the data where the proportions of all identified arteries must sum to 100%. The inferior phrenic artery was defined as the reference category. 

# Initiation

Upload initiation file

```{r}
getwd()
setwd(path)
source('r/777_initiation.R')

data_counts <- na.omit(data_prevalence)
```

Find empirical proportion/count

```{r}
p_hat_pooled <- with(
  data_prevalence,
  sum(n_EHC_patients, na.rm = TRUE) /
    sum(n_patients, na.rm = TRUE)
)

count_hat_pooled <- with(
  data_counts,
  sum(n_EHC, na.rm = TRUE) /
    sum(n_patients, na.rm = TRUE)
)

data_prevalence <- data_prevalence %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    empirical_proportion = n_EHC_patients / n_patients,
    emp_EHCcount_perPat = n_EHC / n_patients
  )
```

# Prevalence

## Show data

```{r}
kableExtra::kable(
  data_prevalence %>%  
    dplyr::select(-Year) 
  )
```


## Set prior

```{r}
prior_prevalence <- c(
  set_prior(paste0('student_t(3, ', logit(p_hat_pooled), ', 100)'), class = "Intercept"),
  prior(exponential(1), class = "sd")
)
```

## Fit model

```{r}

run2(
  name = 'model_prevalence',
  expr = {
    brm(
      n_EHC_patients | trials(n_patients) ~ 1 + (1 | Autor),
      family = binomial(link = "logit"),
      data = data_prevalence,
      prior = prior_prevalence,
      backend = "cmdstanr",
      seed = seeding,
      cores = 1, chains = 4,
      iter = 6000, warmup = 2000,
      control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95)
    )
    },
  reuse = TRUE
  )

## prior summary
prior_summary(model_prevalence)
```

## Check model

```{r}

## Model summary
summary(model_prevalence)

## Check convergence and posterior distribution
plot(model_prevalence)

##
pp_check(model_prevalence)
```

## Heterogeneity between studies

```{r}

## Tau (SD of random effect on logit scale)
tau <- as_draws_df(model_prevalence)$sd_Autor__Intercept
quantile(tau, c(.025, .5, .975))

## Logistic ICC
I2 <- tau^2 / (tau^2 + (pi^2 / 3))
quantile(I2, c(.025, .5, .975))

## 95% Predictive interval for a true prevalence in a new study
set.seed(seeding)
d <- as_draws_df(model_prevalence)
eta_new <- rnorm(
  length(d$b_Intercept),
  mean = d$b_Intercept,
  sd = d$sd_Autor__Intercept
)

p_new <- inv_logit(eta_new)
quantile(p_new, c(.025, .5, .975))

## Prepare summary info about heterogeneity between studies
fmt_3 <- function(x) sprintf("%.3f", x)
ci_txt <- function(q) paste0(fmt_3(q[2]), " [", fmt_3(q[1]), ", ", fmt_3(q[3]), "]")

tau_ci <- quantile(tau, c(.025, .5, .975))
I2_ci <- quantile(I2, c(.025, .5, .975))
pi_ci <- quantile(p_new, c(.025, .5, .975))

note_tau <- paste0(
  "Between-study SD τ (logit scale): ",
  ci_txt(tau_ci),
  "."
)

note_I2 <- paste0(
  "Logistic ICC (I², latent-scale approximation): ", ci_txt(I2_ci), "."
)

note_pi <- paste0(
  "95% predictive interval for true prevalence in a new study: ",
  ci_txt(pi_ci),
  "."
)
```

Between-study heterogeneity was quantified by $\tau$, defined as the standard deviation of the study-specific random intercepts on the logit scale. Posterior samples of $\tau$ were obtained directly from the fitted hierarchical model, and uncertainty was summarized using the median and the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of the posterior distribution.

$I^2$ was calculated as an approximate heterogeneity index on the latent logit scale using the variance of the logistic distribution. Specifically, with between-study heterogeneity $\tau^2$ defined as the variance of the study-specific random intercepts, we computed $I^2 = \frac{\tau^2}{\tau^2 + \pi^2/3}$. This measure represents the proportion of total variance in the linear predictor $\text{logit}(p)$ attributable to between-study heterogeneity and should be interpreted as a latent-scale approximation applicable to binomial models with a logit link.

The between-study variability in prevalence was further summarized using a 95% predictive interval for the true underlying prevalence in a new study. For each posterior draw, a study-specific logit-prevalence was generated as $\eta_{\text{new}}=\mu+u_{\text{new}}$, where $\mu$ denotes the global intercept and $u_{\text{new}}\sim\mathcal N(0,\tau^2)$ represents a random effect for a hypothetical new study. These values were transformed to the prevalence scale using the inverse-logit function, and the predictive interval was defined by the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of the resulting distribution.

## Tabular results

```{r}
nd <- data.frame(
  Autor = unique(data_prevalence$Autor),
  n_patients = 1
)

fit <- fitted(
  model_prevalence,
  newdata = nd,
  re_formula = NULL,
  scale = "response",
  summary = TRUE
)

ran_effs <- data.frame(
  Autor = nd$Autor,
  fit[, c("Estimate", "Q2.5", "Q97.5")]
)

pooled_row <- data.frame(
  Autor = "Pooled estimate",
  Estimate = inv_logit(fixef(model_prevalence)["Intercept", "Estimate"]),
  Q2.5 = inv_logit(fixef(model_prevalence)["Intercept", "Q2.5"]),
  Q97.5 = inv_logit(fixef(model_prevalence)["Intercept", "Q97.5"])
)

tr <- rbind(ran_effs, pooled_row) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Prev_empirical = c(data_prevalence$empirical_proportion, p_hat_pooled),
    N = c(data_prevalence$n_patients, sum(data_prevalence$n_patients)),
    N_EHC = c(data_prevalence$n_EHC_patients, sum(data_prevalence$n_EHC_patients))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    Prev_model_est = Estimate
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Autor, N, N_EHC, Prev_empirical, Prev_model_est, everything()
  )

tr %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    dplyr::across(
      where(is.numeric),
      ~ round(.x, 3)
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    `Estimated prevalence [95% CrI]` = paste0(
      Prev_model_est, " [", `Q2.5`, ", ", `Q97.5`, "]"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    `Observed prevalence` = `Prev_empirical`
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Autor, N, `Observed prevalence`, `Estimated prevalence [95% CrI]`
  ) %>%
  kableExtra::kable(
    align = "lrrr",
    caption = 'Observed and model-estimated prevalence of patients with EHC across included studies. For each study, the table reports the sample size (N), the empirical prevalence, and the study-specific posterior median prevalence with 95% credible intervals (CrI) obtained from a Bayesian hierarchical binomial model with a logit link and a random intercept for study. The pooled estimate corresponds to the prevalence in a typical study (random intercept equal to zero). Between-study heterogeneity is summarized by the standard deviation of the random intercepts (τ) on the logit scale and by an approximate latent-scale intraclass correlation coefficient (I²). The 95% predictive interval represents the expected range of the true underlying prevalence in a new study, reflecting between-study heterogeneity rather than sampling uncertainty.'
    ) %>%
  kableExtra::footnote(
    general = c(note_tau, note_I2, note_pi),
    general_title = "",
    threeparttable = TRUE
  ) %>% 
    kableExtra::kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
    font_size = 12
  )

```

## Forest plot

```{r, fig.height=5, fig.width=7}
#| fig-cap: "Forest plot of EHC prevalence. Error bars represent 95% credible intervals (CrI) based on a mixed-effects binomial regression model, while crosses (x) represent empirical proportions. The size of the points reflects the study sample size (N)."
#| 
plot_data <- tr %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Autor = factor(
      Autor,
      levels = c(
        "Pooled estimate",
        data_prevalence$Autor[order(
          data_prevalence$Year,
          decreasing = TRUE
        )]
      )
    ),
    is_pooled = dplyr::if_else(
      Autor == "Pooled estimate",
      "Pooled",
      "Study"
    )
  )

forest_plot <- ggplot(
  plot_data,
  aes(
    x = Prev_model_est,
    y = Autor
  )
) +
  geom_vline(
    data = dplyr::filter(
      plot_data,
      Autor == "Pooled estimate"
    ),
    aes(xintercept = Prev_model_est),
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "grey40"
  ) +
  geom_errorbarh(
    aes(
      xmin = Q2.5,
      xmax = Q97.5,
      color = is_pooled
    ),
    height = 0.2,
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(
      size = N,
      color = is_pooled
    )
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(x = Prev_empirical),
    shape = 4,
    size = 4,
    alpha = 0.6,
    color = "black"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Study" = "grey20",
      "Pooled" = "firebrick"
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
    limits = c(0, NA),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Prevalence of EHC (95% CrI)",
    y = NULL,
    size = "Sample size (N)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.title.x = element_text(
      size = 12
    ),
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      size = 11
    ),
    axis.text.y = element_text(
      size = 11,
      face = dplyr::if_else(
        levels(plot_data$Autor) == "Pooled estimate",
        "bold",
        "plain"
      )
    ),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11)
  ) +
  guides(color = "none")

forest_plot
```


# Number of ECC per a patient

## Set prior 

```{r}
prior_count <- c(
  set_prior(paste0('student_t(3, ', log(count_hat_pooled), ', 100)'), class = "Intercept"),
  prior(exponential(1), class = "sd")
)
```

## Fit models

```{r}

run2(
  name = "model_EHC_count",
  expr = {
    brm(
      n_EHC ~ 1 + offset(log(n_patients)) + (1 | Autor),
      family = poisson(link = "log"),
      data = data_prevalence %>% na.omit(),
      prior = prior_count,
      backend = "cmdstanr",
      seed = seeding,
      cores = 1, chains = 4,
      iter = 6000, warmup = 2000,
      control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95),
      save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE)
    )
  },
  reuse = TRUE
)

run2(
  name = "model_EHC_count_negbin",
  expr = {
    brm(
      n_EHC ~ 1 + offset(log(n_patients)) + (1 | Autor),
      family = negbinomial(link = "log"),
      data = data_prevalence %>% na.omit(),
      prior = prior_count,
      backend = "cmdstanr",
      seed = seeding,
      cores = 1, chains = 4,
      iter = 6000, warmup = 2000,
      control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99),
      save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE)
    )
  },
  reuse = TRUE
)

## prior summary
prior_summary(model_EHC_count)
prior_summary(model_EHC_count_negbin)
```

## Compare and check models

```{r}
## posterior predictive check
pp_check(model_EHC_count)
pp_check(model_EHC_count_negbin)

## model comparisons
run2(
  name = "loo_pois",
  loo(model_EHC_count, moment_match = TRUE, reloo = TRUE)
)

run2(
  name = "loo_nb",
  loo(model_EHC_count_negbin, moment_match = TRUE, reloo = TRUE)
)

loo_compare(loo_pois, loo_nb)

## Model summary
summary(model_EHC_count)

## Check convergence and posterior distribution
plot(model_EHC_count)
```

Approximate leave-one-out cross-validation with moment matching and exact refits for problematic observations (reloo) showed no improvement in predictive performance of the negative binomial model compared with the Poisson mixed-effects model ($\delta_{elpd}=-0.7$, $SE=1.1$). Posterior predictive checks favoured the Poisson specification, while the negative binomial model exhibited unstable estimation of the dispersion parameter and a non-negligible number of divergent transitions during sampling, indicating poor model fit. The Poisson model was therefore retained as the primary analysis.

## Between-study heterogeneity

```{r}

## Tau (SD of random effect on log scale)
tau <- as_draws_df(model_EHC_count)$sd_Autor__Intercept
quantile(tau, c(.025, .5, .975))
lambda <- exp(d$b_Intercept)

## Poisson VPC
set.seed(seeding)
d <- as_draws_df(model_EHC_count)

mu <- d$b_Intercept
tau <- d$sd_Autor__Intercept

S <- 2000
u <- rnorm(length(mu) * S, 0, rep(tau, each = S))
lam <- exp(rep(mu, each = S) + u)

v_between <- tapply(lam, rep(seq_along(mu), each = S), var)
v_total <- tapply(lam + lam^2, rep(seq_along(mu), each = S), 
                  mean) - tapply(
                    lam, rep(seq_along(mu), each = S
                             ), mean)^2

VPC <- v_between / v_total
quantile(VPC, c(.025, .5, .975))

## 95% Predictive interval for a true count/patient in a new study
set.seed(seeding)
d <- as_draws_df(model_EHC_count)
eta_new <- rnorm(
  length(d$b_Intercept),
  mean = d$b_Intercept,
  sd = d$sd_Autor__Intercept
)

p_new <- exp(eta_new)
quantile(p_new, c(.025, .5, .975))

## Prepare summary info about heterogeneity between studies
fmt_3 <- function(x) sprintf("%.3f", x)
ci_txt <- function(q) paste0(fmt_3(q[2]), " [", fmt_3(q[1]), ", ", fmt_3(q[3]), "]")

tau_ci <- quantile(tau, c(.025, .5, .975))
vpc_ci <- quantile(VPC, c(.025, .5, .975))
pi_ci <- quantile(p_new, c(.025, .5, .975))

note_tau <- paste0(
  "Between-study SD τ (log scale): ",
  ci_txt(tau_ci),
  "."
)

note_vpc <- paste0(
  "Poisson VPC: ",
  ci_txt(vpc_ci),
  "."
)

note_pi <- paste0(
  "95% predictive interval for true count per patient in a new study: ",
  ci_txt(pi_ci),
  "."
)
```

## Set prior

```{r}
y_matrix_old <- data_mult_raw %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Inferior_phrenic_artery,
    Coeliac_trunk_branches,
    SMA_branches,
    Renal_adrenal_arteries,
    IMA,
    Abdominal_wall_artery
  ) %>%
  as.matrix()

col_sums_old <- colSums(y_matrix_old)
col_names_old <- colnames(y_matrix_old)

ref_count_old <- col_sums_old["Inferior_phrenic_artery"]

other_counts_old <- col_sums_old[names(col_sums_old) != "Inferior_phrenic_artery"]
other_names_old <- names(other_counts_old)

calc_multinom_logit <- function(target_count, reference_count) {
  log((target_count + 0.01) / (reference_count + 0.01))
}

prior_intercepts_old <- purrr::map(
  seq_along(other_counts_old),
  function(i) {
    target_val <- other_counts_old[i]
    target_name <- other_names_old[i]
    
    l_val <- calc_multinom_logit(target_val, ref_count_old)
    
    dpar_name <- paste0("mu", gsub("[_.]", "", target_name))
    
    brms::set_prior(
      paste0("student_t(3, ", round(l_val, 3), ", 10)"),
      class = "Intercept",
      dpar = dpar_name
    )
  }
)

prior_multinomial <- c(
  do.call(c, prior_intercepts_old),
  brms::set_prior(
    "exponential(1)",
    class = "sd",
    dpar = paste0("mu", gsub("[_.]", "", other_names_old))
  )
)
```

## Fit model

```{r}

data_model <- data_mult_raw %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Autor, n_EHC2,
    Inferior_phrenic_artery,
    Coeliac_trunk_branches,
    SMA_branches,
    Renal_adrenal_arteries,
    IMA,
    Abdominal_wall_artery
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Y = as.matrix(across(c(
    Inferior_phrenic_artery,
    Coeliac_trunk_branches,
    SMA_branches,
    Renal_adrenal_arteries,
    IMA,
    Abdominal_wall_artery
  ))))

run2(
  name = "model_vessels_multinom",
  expr = {
    brm(
      Y | trials(n_EHC2) ~ 1 + (1 | Autor),
  family = multinomial(link = "logit", refcat = "Inferior_phrenic_artery"),
  data = data_model,
  prior = prior_multinomial,
  backend = "cmdstanr",
  seed = seeding,
  cores = 1, chains = 4,
  iter = 6000, warmup = 2000,
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95)
)
  },
  reuse = TRUE
)

## check prior of the model
prior_summary(model_vessels_multinom)

```

## Between study heterogeneity

```{r}
vessels_all <- c(
  "Inferior_phrenic_artery",
  "Coeliac_trunk_branches",
  "SMA_branches",
  "Renal_adrenal_arteries",
  "IMA",
  "Abdominal_wall_artery"
)

dpars_raw <- c(
  "muCoeliactrunkbranches",
  "muSMAbranches",
  "muRenaladrenalarteries",
  "muIMA",
  "muAbdominalwallartery"
)

draws <- brms::as_draws_df(model_vessels_multinom)

set.seed(seeding)

# 1. Simulace p_new_probs
p_new_probs <- draws %>%
  tibble::as_tibble() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    dplyr::across(
      dplyr::all_of(paste0("b_", dpars_raw, "_Intercept")),
      ~ . + rnorm(
        n(),
        0,
        draws[[gsub("b_", "sd_Autor__", dplyr::cur_column())]]
      ),
      .names = "sim_{.col}"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    dplyr::across(
      dplyr::starts_with("sim_b_mu"),
      ~ exp(.),
      .names = "exp_{.col}"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    exp_sum = 1 + rowSums(
      dplyr::select(
        .,
        dplyr::starts_with("exp_sim_b_mu")
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Inferior_phrenic_artery = 1 / exp_sum
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    dplyr::across(
      dplyr::starts_with("exp_sim_b_mu"),
      ~ . / exp_sum,
      .names = "{.col}_prob"
    )
  )

names(p_new_probs) <- names(p_new_probs) %>%
  gsub("exp_sim_b_mu", "", .) %>%
  gsub("_Intercept_prob", "", .) %>%
  gsub("Coeliactrunkbranches", "Coeliac_trunk_branches", .) %>%
  gsub("SMAbranches", "SMA_branches", .) %>%
  gsub("Renaladrenalarteries", "Renal_adrenal_arteries", .) %>%
  gsub("Abdominalwallartery", "Abdominal_wall_artery", .)

p_new_probs <- p_new_probs %>%
  dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(vessels_all))

pooled_probs <- draws %>%
  tibble::as_tibble() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    dplyr::across(
      dplyr::all_of(paste0("b_", dpars_raw, "_Intercept")),
      ~ exp(.),
      .names = "exp_{.col}"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    sum_exp = 1 + rowSums(dplyr::select(., dplyr::starts_with("exp_b_mu")))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Inferior_phrenic_artery = 1 / sum_exp,
    Coeliac_trunk_branches = exp_b_muCoeliactrunkbranches_Intercept / sum_exp,
    SMA_branches = exp_b_muSMAbranches_Intercept / sum_exp,
    Renal_adrenal_arteries = exp_b_muRenaladrenalarteries_Intercept / sum_exp,
    IMA = exp_b_muIMA_Intercept / sum_exp,
    Abdominal_wall_artery = exp_b_muAbdominalwallartery_Intercept / sum_exp
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(vessels_all))


tau_samples_list <- purrr::map(
  dpars_raw,
  ~ draws[[paste0("sd_Autor__", .x, "_Intercept")]]
)

names(tau_samples_list) <- dpars_raw %>%
  gsub("mu", "", .) %>%
  gsub("Coeliactrunkbranches", "Coeliac_trunk_branches", .) %>%
  gsub("SMAbranches", "SMA_branches", .) %>%
  gsub("Renaladrenalarteries", "Renal_adrenal_arteries", .) %>%
  gsub("Abdominalwallartery", "Abdominal_wall_artery", .)

tau_quantiles <- purrr::map(
  tau_samples_list,
  ~ quantile(.x, c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975))
)

i2_quantiles <- purrr::map(
  tau_samples_list,
  ~ quantile(.x^2 / (.x^2 + (pi^2 / 3)), c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975))
)

p_new_list <- purrr::map(
  p_new_probs,
  ~ quantile(.x, c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975))
)

final_heterogeneity_table <- tibble::tibble(
  vessel = vessels_all
) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    tau_res = purrr::map_chr(
      vessel,
      function(v) {
        if (v %in% names(tau_quantiles)) {
          ci_txt(tau_quantiles[[v]])
        } else {
          NA_character_
        }
      }
    ),
    i2_res = purrr::map_chr(
      vessel,
      function(v) {
        if (v %in% names(i2_quantiles)) {
          ci_txt(i2_quantiles[[v]])
        } else {
          NA_character_
        }
      }
    ),
    pi_res = purrr::map_chr(
      vessel,
      function(v) {
        ci_txt(p_new_list[[v]])
      }
    )
  )

```

## Tabular results of model

```{r}

study_fitted <- fitted(
  model_vessels_multinom,
  newdata = data.frame(Autor = unique(data_mult_raw$Autor), n_EHC2 = 1),
  re_formula = NULL,
  summary = TRUE
)

model_categories <- dimnames(study_fitted)[[3]]

study_estimates_final <- purrr::map_dfc(
  seq_along(model_categories),
  function(i) {
    mat <- study_fitted[, , i]
    
    res <- tibble::tibble(
      !!model_categories[i] := purrr::map_chr(
        seq_len(nrow(mat)),
        function(row_idx) {
          ci_txt(mat[row_idx, c("Q2.5", "Estimate", "Q97.5")])
        }
      )
    )
    return(res)
  }
) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Autor = unique(data_mult_raw$Autor),
    .before = 1
  )

pooled_estimates_wide <- purrr::map_dfc(
  model_categories,
  function(v) {
    clean_v <- gsub("P\\(Y = |\\)", "", v) %>%
      gsub("_", "", .)

    prob_col <- names(pooled_probs)[
      gsub("_", "", names(pooled_probs)) == clean_v
    ]

    if (length(prob_col) == 0) {
       prob_col <- names(pooled_probs)[match(v, names(pooled_probs))]
    }
    
    q <- quantile(
      pooled_probs[[prob_col]], 
      c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975)
    )
    
    tibble::tibble(
      !!v := ci_txt(q)
    )
  }
) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Autor = "Pooled estimate",
    .before = 1
  )

final_table <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  study_estimates_final,
  pooled_estimates_wide
)

clean_colnames <- names(final_table) %>%
  gsub("P\\(Y = ", "", .) %>%
  gsub("\\)", "", .) %>%
  gsub("_", " ", .)


final_table %>%
  kableExtra::kable(
    col.names = clean_colnames,
    align = c("l", rep("r", length(model_categories))),
    caption = "Model-estimated proportions [95% CrI] of arterial sources for EHC, based on a Bayesian hierarchical multinomial model with a logit link and a random intercept for study"
  ) %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
    font_size = 12
  ) %>%
  kableExtra::footnote(
    general = c(
      "Heterogeneity summary:",
      purrr::map_chr(
        seq_len(nrow(final_heterogeneity_table)),
        function(i) {
          row <- final_heterogeneity_table[i, ]
          paste0(
            gsub("_", " ", row$vessel), ": τ=", 
            ifelse(is.na(row$tau_res), "-", row$tau_res),
            "; I²=", ifelse(is.na(row$i2_res), "-", row$i2_res),
            "; PI=", row$pi_res
          )
        }
      )
    ),
    general_title = "",
    threeparttable = TRUE
  )
```

## Between study heterogeneity

```{r}
vessels_all <- vessels_spec
dpars_spec <- dpars_new

draws <- brms::as_draws_df(model_vessels_multinom_spec)

set.seed(seeding)

# 2. AUTOMATICKÁ DETEKCE PARAMETRŮ Z MODELU
# Najde všechny parametry začínající "b_mu" a končící "Intercept"
all_b_names <- colnames(draws)
dpars_raw_full <- grep("^b_mu.*_Intercept$", all_b_names, value = TRUE)
# Očistíme na čisté dpars (např. "muCoeliactrunkbranches")
dpars_raw <- gsub("^b_|_Intercept$", "", dpars_raw_full)

set.seed(seeding)

# --- 3. SIMULACE P_NEW_PROBS ---
p_new_probs <- draws %>%
  tibble::as_tibble() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    dplyr::across(
      dplyr::all_of(paste0("b_", dpars_raw, "_Intercept")),
      ~ . + rnorm(n(), 0, draws[[gsub("b_", "sd_Autor__", dplyr::cur_column())]]),
      .names = "sim_{.col}"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    dplyr::across(dplyr::starts_with("sim_b_mu"), ~ exp(.), .names = "exp_{.col}")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    exp_sum = 1 + rowSums(dplyr::select(., dplyr::starts_with("exp_sim_b_mu")))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Inferior_phrenic_artery = 1 / exp_sum
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    dplyr::across(
      dplyr::starts_with("exp_sim_b_mu"),
      ~ . / exp_sum,
      .names = "{.col}_prob"
    )
  )

clean_names_map <- setNames(vessels_all, gsub("_", "", vessels_all))

fix_names <- function(x) {

  clean_key <- gsub("exp_sim_b_mu|_Intercept_prob", "", x)

  if (clean_key %in% names(clean_names_map)) {
    return(clean_names_map[[clean_key]])
  }
  return(x)
}

names(p_new_probs) <- sapply(names(p_new_probs), fix_names)
p_new_probs <- p_new_probs %>% dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(vessels_all))


pooled_probs <- draws %>%
  tibble::as_tibble() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(paste0("b_", dpars_raw, "_Intercept")), ~ exp(.), .names = "exp_{.col}")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    sum_exp = 1 + rowSums(dplyr::select(., dplyr::starts_with("exp_b_mu")))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Inferior_phrenic_artery = 1 / sum_exp
  )


for (dpar in dpars_raw) {
  raw_id <- gsub("mu", "", dpar)
  nice_name <- clean_names_map[[raw_id]]
  pooled_probs[[nice_name]] <- pooled_probs[[paste0("exp_b_", dpar, "_Intercept")]] / pooled_probs$sum_exp
}

pooled_probs <- pooled_probs %>% dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(vessels_all))


tau_samples_list <- purrr::map(
  dpars_raw, ~ draws[[paste0("sd_Autor__", .x, "_Intercept")]]
  )
names(tau_samples_list) <- sapply(gsub("mu", "", dpars_raw), function(x) clean_names_map[[x]])

tau_quantiles <- purrr::map(tau_samples_list, ~ quantile(.x, c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975)))
i2_quantiles  <- purrr::map(tau_samples_list, ~ quantile(.x^2 / (.x^2 + (pi^2 / 3)), c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975)))
p_new_list    <- purrr::map(p_new_probs,      ~ quantile(.x, c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975)))

final_heterogeneity_table <- tibble::tibble(vessel = vessels_all) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    tau_res = purrr::map_chr(vessel, ~ if (.x %in% names(tau_quantiles)) ci_txt(tau_quantiles[[.x]]) else NA_character_),
    i2_res  = purrr::map_chr(vessel, ~ if (.x %in% names(i2_quantiles)) ci_txt(i2_quantiles[[.x]]) else NA_character_),
    pi_res  = purrr::map_chr(vessel, ~ ci_txt(p_new_list[[.x]]))
  )
```

## Tabular results of model

```{r}

study_fitted <- fitted(
  model_vessels_multinom_spec,
  newdata = data.frame(Autor = unique(data_mult_spec$Autor), n_EHC2 = 1),
  re_formula = NULL,
  summary = TRUE
)

model_categories <- dimnames(study_fitted)[[3]]

study_estimates_final <- purrr::map_dfc(
  seq_along(model_categories),
  function(i) {
    mat <- study_fitted[, , i]
    
    res <- tibble::tibble(
      !!model_categories[i] := purrr::map_chr(
        seq_len(nrow(mat)),
        function(row_idx) {
          ci_txt(mat[row_idx, c("Q2.5", "Estimate", "Q97.5")])
        }
      )
    )
    return(res)
  }
) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Autor = unique(data_mult_spec$Autor),
    .before = 1
  )

pooled_estimates_wide <- purrr::map_dfc(
  model_categories,
  function(v) {
    clean_v <- gsub("P\\(Y = |\\)", "", v) %>%
      gsub("_", "", .)

    prob_col <- names(pooled_probs)[
      gsub("_", "", names(pooled_probs)) == clean_v
    ]

    if (length(prob_col) == 0) {
       prob_col <- names(pooled_probs)[match(v, names(pooled_probs))]
    }
    
    q <- quantile(
      pooled_probs[[prob_col]], 
      c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975)
    )
    
    tibble::tibble(
      !!v := ci_txt(q)
    )
  }
) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Autor = "Pooled estimate",
    .before = 1
  )

final_table <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  study_estimates_final,
  pooled_estimates_wide
)

clean_colnames <- names(final_table) %>%
  gsub("P\\(Y = ", "", .) %>%
  gsub("\\)", "", .) %>%
  gsub("_", " ", .)


final_table %>%
  kableExtra::kable(
    col.names = clean_colnames,
    align = c("l", rep("r", length(model_categories))),
    caption = "Model-estimated proportions [95% CrI] of arterial sources for EHC, based on a Bayesian hierarchical multinomial model with a logit link and a random intercept for study"
  ) %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
    font_size = 12
  ) %>%
  kableExtra::footnote(
    general = c(
      "Heterogeneity summary:",
      purrr::map_chr(
        seq_len(nrow(final_heterogeneity_table)),
        function(i) {
          row <- final_heterogeneity_table[i, ]
          paste0(
            gsub("_", " ", row$vessel), ": τ=", 
            ifelse(is.na(row$tau_res), "-", row$tau_res),
            "; I²=", ifelse(is.na(row$i2_res), "-", row$i2_res),
            "; PI=", row$pi_res
          )
        }
      )
    ),
    general_title = "",
    threeparttable = TRUE
  )
```

## Empirical proportions 

```{r}
empirical_data <- data_mult_spec %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Autor,
    n_EHC2,
    dplyr::all_of(vessels_all)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    dplyr::across(
      dplyr::all_of(vessels_all),
      ~ .x / n_EHC2
    )
  )

total_row <- data_mult_spec %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    Autor = "Total / Overall",
    n_EHC2 = sum(n_EHC2),
    dplyr::across(
      dplyr::all_of(vessels_all),
      ~ sum(.x) / sum(n_EHC2)
    )
  )

empirical_final <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  empirical_data,
  total_row
)

clean_empirical_colnames <- names(empirical_final) %>%
  gsub("_", " ", .) %>%
  gsub("n EHC2", "Count of EHCs", .)


empirical_final %>%
  kableExtra::kable(
    col.names = clean_empirical_colnames,
    digits = 3,
    align = c("l", "c", rep("r", length(vessels_all))),
    caption = "Empirical proportions of arterial sources for EHC across included studies."
  ) %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = c(
      "striped",
      "hover",
      "condensed"
    ),
    font_size = 12
  ) %>%
  kableExtra::row_spec(
    nrow(empirical_final),
    bold = TRUE,
    extra_css = "border-top: 2px solid black;"
  )
```
